title: EDDE: Container Deployment Framework Beyond the Cloud
problem: Cloud-oriented container deployment frameworks fail for edge environments: excessive client-registry communication increases RTT; user-space filesystems (FUSE) add substantial I/O overhead; on-demand images stress storage on resource-constrained edge devices.
motivation: Edge services (autonomous driving, edge gaming, HPC/AI-powered applications) require rapid startup and immediate responsiveness. Geographically distributed, heterogeneous edge devices with constrained resources demand edge-optimized deployment solutions.
method: EDDE redesigns the on-demand container image pipeline for edge: reduces client-registry communication latency, optimizes kernel-space I/O handling avoiding FUSE overhead, minimizes storage pressure through efficient image provisioning.
key_novelty: Edge-optimized container framework addressing three key pain points: network latency (minimized registry communication), I/O efficiency (kernel-space I/O vs FUSE overhead), storage efficiency (reduced footprint on constrained devices).
contributions: 9.8× higher deployment efficiency vs standard Docker on edge devices
147% faster container startup vs state-of-the-art on-demand solutions
28% native I/O latency reduction vs FUSE-based approaches
Edge-optimized image pipeline addressing heterogeneous device requirements
limitations: Evaluation limited to edge deployment scenarios
No comparison with alternative container runtimes (containerd, podman)
Limited detail on heterogeneous device support breadth
Abstract-only prevents assessment of edge device types tested
primary_theme: Edge-optimized container deployment via pipeline redesign
